thread:
pagerduty-bot: :rotating_light: Paging production on-call: multiple requests served out of eu-central-1 despite customer data-residency=us-only. Possible routing policy misconfiguration causing region fallback. Impacting ~12 customers. Please ack and escalate.

irina: acked. I'm on it, pulling logs now. Paging Maria for on-call handoff.

maria: oncall here. give me a 1-line summary + what user-facing symptoms are.

irina: summary: smart-routing policy for tenant routing appears to allow cross-region fallback when local capacity low. It looks like the policy that should enforce residency was accidentally set to `defer_to_fallback` instead of `strict`. Symptoms: requests for embeddings/llm completion show region header eu-central-1 in audit logs, customers flagged data residency violation. No crash, just wrong region selection.

leo: seeing the same in the tracer: router decided 'variant-b32-quant' in eu-central-1 was compatible and routed to it after timeout in us-west-2. There's a loop where fallback triggers another fallback policy.

jordan: how many requests? do we have rate?

irina: approx 1.4k requests over the last 18 minutes, ~350 unique tenants, but only 12 tenants have residency=us-only flag set. Confirmed 12 customer audit entries.

maria: immediate mitigation plan: 1) disable cross-region fallback globally for routing policies 2) patch the affected group to `strict residency` 3) notify impacted customers and open support ticket with SLO credits. Any objections?

secops-bot: Security alert: potential compliance breach (data residency). Generating evidence bundle for legal.

ops-runbook-bot: Runbook hint: to disable fallback quickly: `rictl set-global-fallback --mode=off` (admin). To patch a policy: `rictl patch-routing --policy-id=<policy> --set enforce_residency=strict`.

irina: executing step 1 now: `rictl set-global-fallback --mode=off --reason "emergency disable: residency breach"`

maria: oncall takeover at 1763285980 — handing off to me for coordination. I've messaged support to get customer contacts.

leo: verifying change propagation: router cluster shows new config, but one proxy pod still had old cached policy. Running `kubectl rollout restart deploy/route-proxy -n inference` on eu cluster.

jordan: are we sure disabling fallback won't cause timeouts for other tenants?

maria: will increase short-term capacity for us-west to avoid timeouts. Spinning up two extra dedicated workers in us-west-2: `infractl scale capacity --pool us-west-2 --add 2`

irina: patched specific policy for policy-id=rt-9921: `rictl patch-routing --policy-id=rt-9921 --set enforce_residency=strict` — confirmed API returns 200 and policy shows `enforce_residency: strict`.

leo: audit logs now show subsequent requests for those tenants served from us-west-2. No new eu-central-1 hits after restart.

secops-bot: Evidence bundle uploaded to /evidence/incidents/1763285600/ — includes audit logs, routing-config diff, sample request headers (12 tenants).

maria: customer comms drafted: "We detected routing that temporarily routed requests outside your designated region. We've corrected the routing policy and disabled cross-region fallback during investigation. We're preparing a writeup and SLO remediation. If you have regulatory concerns, contact enterprise-support@redwood.ai." Anyone want to review?

jordan: looks good. Add timeline + affected request IDs.

ops-runbook-bot: Suggested timeline fields: detection_ts, mitigation_start_ts, mitigation_end_ts, rollback_ts (if any).

irina: mitigation start: 1763285665, mitigation end (global-fallback off + policy patch + proxy restart finished): 1763286240.

maria: filing an incident ticket: INCIDENT-2026-03-15-01. Assigning postmortem to irina and leo.

leo: root cause analysis notes: config drift introduced during a rolling config update last night. A CRON job that reconciles policy templates mistakenly applied `defer_to_fallback` to policies with `residency=us-only` due to a templating bug: `{{#if use_fallback}}defer_to_fallback{{else}}strict{{/if}}` where `use_fallback` defaulted true for new templates.

irina: mitigation for long term: 1) add a hard guard in runtime that prevents serving out-of-region when tenant has `residency=strict` 2) add unit tests for template rendering 3) add an alert when policy changes to residency for any tenant.

maria: sec/compliance: please prepare a short signed attestation we can send customers (secops + legal).

secops-bot: Noted. SecOps will prepare attestation draft and CC legal.

jordan: any further live mitigation needed?

maria: monitoring: keep an eye on audit logs for 1 hour, and we will keep global-fallback off until the guard is live. Set a follow-up checkpoint in 30m.

ops-runbook-bot: checkpoint scheduled: 1763288185 (30m).

irina: quick post-action: created PR to runtime guard: `runtime: prevent_cross_region_for_strict_residency` — PR#4238. Running tests.

leo: I've drafted the support messages and opened support tickets for the 12 customers, linking the evidence bundle.

maria: thanks team. Final note: this was contained to a config drift + fallback logic. No data exfil or access outside routing — just wrong region selection. We'll keep global-fallback off until runtime guard is merged and deployed.

pagerduty-bot: Incident acknowledged by maria, irina, leo. Status: mitigated (routing corrected).

maria: closing on-call loop. Postmortem owners: irina (ops), leo (runtime). I'll coordinate comms.

irina: adding meeting to calendar: "INCIDENT-2026-03-15-01 postmortem" — invite sent.

jordan: thanks all. :thumbsup:

maria: closing thread; will post final postmortem link here when ready.
